newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian court suspends arrest warrant against Rao.
newsitem.headline: Indian court suspends arrest warrant against Rao.

text.p: An Indian court on Friday suspended a warrant for the arrest of former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao until a hearing next week, a lawyer representing Rao said.
Counsel R.K. Anand told Reuters that the Delhi High Court issued the stay order after a lower court judge had issued arrest warrants against Rao and three others in a seven-year-old forgery case.
The Delhi High Court scheduled a hearing for October 7 on Rao's request that the arrest warrant be quashed.
Earlier on Friday, a judge issued arrest warrants against Rao and three others in the forgery case.

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), India's federal police, charged Rao and three others on September 26 in the forgery case involving an alleged attempt in 1989 to tarnish the reputation of V.P. Singh, an opposition leader who later became prime minister.

Rao stepped down as Congress leader last month after a judge upheld a summons ordering him to appear in court in a separate criminal conspiracy case. He remains leader of Congress's delegation in parliament.
